name: Treadmill exhaustion test
description: The animal runs on a motorized treadmill at a constant or increasing speed until exhaustion. Assesses endurance and exercise capacity.

parameters.label: Lane length
parameters.help: Length of the running lane, from the front wall to the rear grid.

parameters.label: Exhaustion time on the grid
parameters.help: Continuous time on the shock grid that defines exhaustion: the subject no longer returns to the belt.

parameters.label: Minimum grid contact
parameters.help: A stay on the shock grid counts as a shock only when it lasts at least this long; shorter contacts are ignored.

parameters.label: Maximum tracking gap
parameters.help: Longest tracking dropout that is bridged; movement across a longer gap is excluded. Increase only for low-frame-rate videos.

parameters.label: Accelerating protocol
parameters.help: On: the belt accelerates from the start speed to the end speed. Off: the belt runs at the start speed throughout the trial.

parameters.label: Start speed
parameters.help: Belt speed at the start of the trial.

parameters.label: End speed
parameters.help: Belt speed reached at the end of the acceleration phase and held thereafter. Must not be lower than the start speed.

parameters.label: Acceleration duration
parameters.help: Time over which the belt speed rises linearly from the start speed to the end speed.

parameters.label: Cut-off time
parameters.help: The trial ends at this time even if the subject is still running.

zones.label: Shock grid
zones.geometry: Polygon drawn on the side view over the shock grid at the back of the lane.

events.label: Exhaustion
events.definition: A stay on the grid is a run of contiguous counted intervals whose earlier sample lies in the shock grid zone. Exhaustion is placed at the start of the first stay that lasts at least exhaustion_dwell_s.

events.label: Shock
events.definition: A stay on the grid is a run of contiguous counted intervals whose earlier sample lies in the shock grid zone. A shock is placed at the start of every stay that lasts at least min_shock_dwell_s.

metrics.label: Time to exhaustion
metrics.description: Time until the subject meets the exhaustion criterion; longer times indicate greater endurance.
metrics.definition: Coordinates are in centimeters in the calibration's side view of the lane: x along the lane from the shock grid end (x = 0) to the front (x = lane_length_cm), y vertical. Samples after max_trial_duration_s are ignored. A counted interval is a pair of consecutive tracked samples separated by 0 < dt <= max_sample_gap_s. Time of the exhaustion event, if it occurs by the cut-off time.
metrics.missingWhen: Missing (NO_VALID_INTERVALS) when there are no counted intervals, (EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED) when the recording covers max_trial_duration_s without exhaustion, and (INCOMPLETE_RECORDING) when a shorter recording ends without exhaustion.

metrics.label: Running time
metrics.description: Time spent running, until exhaustion or the cut-off time.
metrics.definition: The run ends at the exhaustion event or, without exhaustion, at the end of the recording, censored at max_trial_duration_s.
metrics.formula: exhaustion time, else min(recording duration, max_trial_duration_s)
metrics.missingWhen: Missing (NO_VALID_INTERVALS) when there are no counted intervals.

metrics.label: Distance run
metrics.description: Distance covered on the treadmill during the run; longer distances indicate greater endurance.
metrics.definition: Integral of belt speed over the running time; the speed rises linearly from the start speed to the end speed over acceleration_duration_s and then remains constant.
metrics.formula: integral of speed(t) dt over [0, run_time_s]
metrics.missingWhen: Missing (NO_VALID_INTERVALS) when there are no counted intervals.

metrics.label: Shock count
metrics.description: Number of shocks or rear-grid contacts during the run; more shocks suggest fatigue or low motivation.
metrics.definition: Shock events strictly before the end of the run.
metrics.missingWhen: Missing (NO_VALID_INTERVALS) when there are no counted intervals.
